narrative:
**Engagement pulled back sharply while the model population kept growing.** Aggregate model downloads fell 31.6% week over week to 2,847,321 across 23,577 tracked models, the largest single move in the dataset. Likes softened more modestly: model likes fell 9.3% to 11,848 and Space likes fell 10.0% to 1,184 across 6,400 Spaces. The decline in downloads was not matched by a contraction in supply — Qwen-family models rose 19.6% to 5,950 and other-open rose 2.9% to 5,784, while Llama fell 40.6% to 1,033, NVIDIA Nemotron fell 56.8% to 98, and DeepSeek fell 49.7% to 94. One important caveat: 9,712 of 23,577 models (41%) were classified as "unknown" family, up 24.4% week over week, so family-level counts should be read as a lower bound and shifts may partly reflect attribution rather than real churn.

**On the Spaces side, coding was the standout mover.** Coding Spaces rose 30.9% to 305, lifting coding's share of all Spaces to 4.77% (+27.3%), with document-AI up 10.8% to 431, scientific-tools up 11.9% to 254, and chat-assistant — still the largest named category at 1,047 Spaces — up 7.5%. Robotics fell 32.9% to 55 Spaces, the sharpest decline among use cases. Within the family mix for coding (n=181 Spaces), Qwen remained the plurality at 34.3% despite a 25.4% relative drop, while DeepSeek rose to 7.7% (+74.0%) and proprietary-API references rose to 10.5% (+136.2%). Image generation showed a similar pattern, with Qwen at 26.4% (+74.3%) and proprietary APIs at 2.6% (+225.3%) of 417 Spaces. Family-share splits for 3D-gaming (n=23), education (n=27), and robotics (n=16) rest on very small bases and individual sub-family cells there are too few to report reliably.

**Technology and vertical penetration moved in opposite directions across adjacent themes.** Tool-use penetration rose 15.8% to 4.38% of Spaces and diffusion rose 9.5% to 5.28%, while RAG fell 28.6% to 2.08% and fine-tuned fell 22.6% to 2.75%. Among verticals, cybersecurity rose 47.0% to 2.95% and legal rose 35.9% to 1.70% — both off small bases of roughly 189 and 109 Spaces — while healthcare fell 22.8% to 3.55% and scientific-research fell 11.5% to 7.14%. SDK mix held broadly steady, with static Spaces at 3,571 (+2.2%) and Gradio at 2,210 (+5.8%). Note that only 1-week deltas were available this cycle; 4-week and 12-week baselines were null, so none of these moves can yet be separated from normal weekly noise. Next week, watch whether the 31.6% download drop reverses or persists into a second week, which would distinguish a one-off collection artifact from a genuine engagement decline.
